correctness.rationale: Veerman–Oberly–Fox Eq. (2.1), Eqs. (3.1)–(3.2) and Theorem 3.3 give the required ensemble, mechanical-word indexing, closed-support component and weight k/(2^k−1). The unique numerator-one digit is at k−1. Denominators 2 and 3 have lower support distance 1/4 and cannot contribute for u>10. The decreasing lower endpoints for k≥4 give K, and every numerator-one term between K and 3u/2 also meets its upper support bound. A higher numerator contributing below 3u/2 would have to equal 2 with tau>1/2 and k>u; its first digit is zero for these k, contradicting that inequality. Both the added numerator-one tail and the omitted higher numerators are thus bounded in absolute sum by a constant times the tail of k²2^(−k) from 3u/2. Replacing the surviving tail by k2^(−k) costs O(K4^(−K)), and its exact geometric sum is (K+1)2^(1−K). For q=floor(u), the lower support bound first holds at q or q+1, and at q exactly up to and including q/(1−2^(1−q)). Normalization leaves 2^(u−K) times the asserted relative error. Integer u, u=q+q^(−1/2), and u=q+theta for fixed 0<theta<1 realize the two ends and the interior of [1/2,1]; the phase bounds exclude other limits. This is for the specified closed-interval representative. The finite rational checker was inspected, not run or used for the infinite estimates. The printed prior Proposition 5.2 has a reciprocal-integer coefficient discrepancy: its stated 2q2^(−q) with exponentially smaller error omits 2^(1−q), which is present in its own proof and here. The frozen proof uses the exact component formula, not that misstated estimate.
